doc.title: Jones Hank — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

title: The two Franks, Ernie Wilkins and the Basie arrangers
summary: Jones links Frank Foster, Frank Wess and Ernie Wilkins from Detroit and Basie's band full of arrangers.

story.theme_name: Playing with Count Basie: joining, leading, leaving
story.community_name: Playing with Count Basie: the band, its feel and its people

blocks.x: You seem to have a special relationship over the years with the two Franks.

Yes, that’s quite true. I mentioned earlier, Frank Foster was a member of that band at the Three Sixes in Detroit on Adam’s street. I didn’t see him much from that period until he became a member of the Count Basie band along with Wes. The two Franks were in Basie’s band together along with Thad and Graham or Leonard— some other arrangers. Also, Ernie Wilkins. It was a band full of arrangers.
Ernie Wilkins is another name that keeps popping up in your career.
Ernie did a lot dates for Savoy at Rudy Van Gelder’s out in Hackensack.
Yes, but I did not know that at the time. There again, there's that Detroit school.
There it is! Over and over again.
He probably went to CasTech along with some of those other guys.
